item.title: It took one game for Cam Skattebo to renege on promise to stop backflipping: ‘It brings juice to this team’

Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Backflipping to Cam Skattebo seems to be a forbidden fruit. He's acknowledged he probably shouldn't do it . But when the adrenaline is flowing, he just can't help himself. Last week, the Giants ' young running back caught the attention of fans when he vowed to end his go-to celebration, saying that Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL on a sack celebration was a wake-up call. That didn't last long. Days after his anti-flipping commitment, after picking up a key first down for the Giants in their win over the Jaguars on Sunday, Skattebo was airborne. item.title: Virginia Tech basketball: Hokies lose first game to Oklahoma State after terrible second half
item.description: SIOUX CITY, IOWA - NOVEMBER 10: Ben Hammond #3 of the Virginia Tech Hokies drives against Isaia Howard #23 of the Iowa Hawkeyes during the first half at Tyson Events Center on November 10, 2026 in Sioux City, Iowa. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 6-0 Virginia Tech Hokies were back Sunday in the Shriners Children’s Charleston Classic in Charleston, South Carolina. The opponent: the Oklahoma State Cowboys. After a back-and-forth first half with the lead changing often, the Cowboys took control in the second half, outscoring the Hokies 65-39 in the final 20 minutes to win 106-80. Remarkably, this game was tied at halftime. Both teams were hot from the field, with OSU shooting 59% and the Hokies 47% in the first half. Tech made 8-of-15 (53%) from beyond the arc in the first half, while the Cowboys made 5-of-10. While the Hokies cooled off in the second half, Oklahoma State only got hotter. VT made only 11 of 28 field-goal attempts in the second half, including 4-for-14 from the 3-point line, while the Cowboys shot an unheard-of 74% in the second half. And there you have it, that’s the game. The back-and-forth action from the first half carried into the second half. However, back-to-back buckets from Ben Hammond and Amani Hansberry at the 16:31 mark gave the Hokies a 54-51 lead. The crowd sensed the tide might be turning in Virginia Tech’s favor. Instead, it spurred a run by the Cowboys that opened up the game. Oklahoma State scored the next 11 points to build an 8-point lead. The Cowboys never looked back. After a Hammond 3-pointer and two Jaylen Curry free throws cut the lead back to 64-59, OSU scored 13 in a row to blow it wide open. Virginia Tech finishes the weekend 1-1 in Charleston, suffering its first loss of the season. Next up for Virginia Tech is a date with Old Dominion at Cassell Coliseum on Friday. Hammond led the Hokies with 24 points and five rebounds. He was phenomenal as usual, but he had little help. Curry scored 18, but in playing against his former team, he let his emotions get the best of him early, starting down Oklahoma State coach Steve Lutz. Mike Young and Lutz quickly went head-to-head, but it ended as fast as it began, and both coaches laughed it off. Curry led the Hokies with 7 assists, but exhibited poor shot selection at times. Hansberry had a rough game, finishing with 9 points and 6 rebounds and making only 3-of-10 from the field. OSU outrebounded the Hokies 33-27 and Tech had 11 turnovers. Virginia Tech’s continued insistence on living by the 3-point shot can sometimes haunt them. It did on Sunday. Plus, when another team shoots 74% in a half, it’s hard to beat them. The good news is that rarely happens.

item.description: Aug 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; The NFL shield logo on the field at SoFi Stadium. Before a single snap was played, though, the crowd made sure that the night would be remembered for more than just football. As Mexican singer Majo Aguilar performed the Mexican national anthem, the entire stadium sang along with her in a moment that quickly went viral. Fans and media members alike were blown away, with many saying it gave them chills. ‘A MUST LISTEN’ The NFL announced back in September that Aguilar would sing the Mexican national anthem, while Oakland-born singer-songwriter MXKA would perform the U.S. national anthem. Aguilar, a member of Mexico’s famed Aguilar music family and a cousin of Ángela Aguilar, has more than 533 million global streams and also sang the anthem as part of Telemundo’s World Cup coverage. “I feel very happy to be able to perform the Mexican National Anthem. Mexico is a beautiful country with a rich culture,” Aguilar said in the NFL’s announcement . “Thank you to the NFL for inviting me to be part of such a special moment and allowing me to represent my country. It fills me with pride to be Mexican.” Needless to say, she and the crowd delivered. Video of the performance shared by SportsCenter racked up more than 500,000 views within a couple of hours, and plenty of people chimed in with their reactions. item.description: Sometimes, the most entertaining part of hockey games is the fights on the ice between players . item.title: Jaguars defense tougher as game wore on, but didn't get the stop it needed
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars defense played well enough to win on Nov. 22 against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium Even Jaguars coach Liam Coen , whose offense simply wasn't up to the task, admitted as much after the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants . "They gave us plenty of opportunities," Coen said about his defense. "We didn't play complementary football. We turned it over, they scored points. We get turnovers, we didn't score points. I felt like you hold a team to 23 points in the National Football League, you should win some of those games." But not this one. There were some heartening aspects about how the Jags played defense against the Giants. Edge rusher Josh Hines-Allen got his first solo sack since opening week, forced a fumble and batted down a pass. Safety Antonio Johnson had a big fumble return and came an eyelash away from an interception on the Giants' next offensive play. New additions Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux on the defensive line helped the Jags hold New York running backs to 2.6 yards per carry and the Giants had only 77 yards rushing, nearly half on scrambles by quarterback J.J. McCarthy. The Jaguars defense played especially well during a dominating sequence of four second-half possessions in a row in which McCarthy and his two key weapons, running back Cam Skattebo and wide receiver Malik Nabers, were simply squashed. Jags defense produced opportunities for offense New York moved the ball on its first two possessions of the second half, but Dominic Zvada hooked a 32-yard field goal attempt, and Johnson scooped up a fumble forced by Hines-Allen and returned it 42 yards to the Giants' 31 after McCarthy had moved his offense to the Jags' 32. The Jaguars offense failed to take advantage of either opportunity. They had to punt after the missed field goal and Trevor Lawrence threw an incomplete pass on fourth-and-one at the New York 11 following Johnson's turnover. The defense only redoubled their efforts after that. On New York's next four possessions, McCarthy was 1 of 11, and his completion went for only 8 yards. The Giants had 11 total yards on those possessions. The Giants also beat themselves, including a holding penalty on guard Francis Mauigoa nullifying McCarthy's 29-yard scramble. The biggest self-inflicted wound came after an 8-yard pass to Nabers. Travis Hunter made the tackle but was hit late by center Ben Hudson, drawing an unnecessary roughness flag. Instead of second-and-two, the dead-ball penalty made it third-and-17 and safety Jessie Bates III blitzed to force McCarthy into an completion. Aside from that, it was all Jaguars. New York didn't get a first down on those possessions and got three points on one, Zvada's 43-yard field goal, thanks to the Jaguars' offense: Lawrence was intercepted for the second time, and Paulson Abedo returned it to the Jags' 28. item.title: Gene Steratore questions review process in Giants-Jaguars
item.description: Credit: NBC, CBS The New York Giants upset the Jacksonville Jaguars in one of the most stunning results of the NFL’s Week 11 Sunday slate. After carrying a 20–6 lead into the fourth quarter, the Giants were able to hold off a late charge from the Jaguars and secure the win at home by a score of 23–18. But it’s possible the game could have had a different outcome had one close call gone in the Jaguars’ favor. The call in question came with 12 minutes left to play and the Jaguars driving in Giants territory. Facing third-and-9, Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw a dart to receiver Parker Washington, who appeared to come down with the ball right on the line in the back of the end zone, but the play was ruled an incompletion on the field. The Jaguars challenged the incomplete call, and as the broadcast watched the replays in slow motion, it seemed pretty clear that Washington caught the ball, controlled it, and got two feet in bounds for the score. “At this point, when Parker Washington after the bobble possesses that football, I still had the right foot down as he’s falling, then I have the left foot touch,” rules analyst Gene Steratore told the broadcast booth. “I see the ball move a little bit, but I did not think that he lost possession of the football. You can clearly see at this point, I have possession, right foot down, tap with the left foot. Yes, does the ball move a little, but the right hand in my opinion continues to keep that secure enough that I would say in my opinion, that is a ball movement, but he is still controlling that football. I think it’s a touchdown.” But the people that control the replay reviews didn’t agree with Steratore, and the call of incomplete that was made on the field stood. The Jaguars would settle for a field goal, cutting the lead to 20–9. “I did not think he lost possession of the football… I think it’s a touchdown, fellas.” CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore disagreed with this being ruled incomplete after review on a potential Parker Washington TD for the Jaguars. https://t.co/4RdlPYAYXQ — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 23, 2026 Later on in the broadcast, Steratore reported on the conversation he had with the league office explaining the reasoning behind the decision. “They felt like there was not enough clear and obvious evidence to change the ruling on the field, which was an incomplete pass. item.title: Texas Football Could Deliver a Major SEC Championship Statement Before Alabama Even Takes the Field
item.description: Oct 17, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns Head Coach Steve Sarkisian during the first half against the Florida Gators at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) COLLEGE STATION, Texas — Texas has an opportunity to make the Southeastern Conference’s championship race considerably less complicated before Saturday’s games even begin. The Longhorns visit Texas A&M on Friday, Nov. 27, with a potential trip to Atlanta hanging in the balance. Meanwhile, Alabama and Tennessee must wait until Saturday to complete their conference schedules. That timing could prove important. If the right results fall into place Friday, Texas could secure the second SEC Championship Game berth before either of its competitors takes the field. Texas has an opportunity to seize control Texas (9-2, 6-2 SEC) enters Rivalry Week tied with Alabama and Tennessee for second place. Georgia has already secured the conference’s first championship game berth. However, Texas holds several favorable tiebreaking advantages. The Longhorns defeated Tennessee 20-17 earlier this season. Additionally, Texas holds an advantage over Alabama based on results against common SEC opponents. Those results provide Texas with a favorable path if the conference race produces a two-team tie. The Egg Bowl could play an unexpected role Texas’ championship hopes also depend on the outcome of a rivalry game involving two other SEC programs. Ole Miss hosts Mississippi State at noon Friday, several hours before Texas visits Texas A&M. If Ole Miss defeats Mississippi State and Texas subsequently beats the Aggies, the Longhorns would clinch a championship game berth regardless of Saturday’s results. That scenario involves the SEC’s opponents’ winning percentage tiebreaker. Consequently, a game in Oxford could help determine whether Texas plays for a conference championship in Atlanta. Texas A&M has plenty of motivation Texas A&M (4-7, 1-7 SEC) enters the matchup with a disappointing conference record. However, the Aggies have an opportunity to deny their biggest rival a potential championship appearance. That possibility adds another layer to an already emotional rivalry. A Texas victory would improve the Longhorns to 10-2 and strengthen their College Football Playoff résumé. Meanwhile, a loss would eliminate Texas from the SEC Championship Game race. For Steve Sarkisian’s program, Friday represents an opportunity to finish the regular season with a statement. For Texas A&M, it represents an opportunity to make sure its rival does not get that satisfaction. And depending on what happens earlier in Oxford, the Longhorns might enter Kyle Field knowing exactly what a victory would mean. item.title: Eric Garcia reveals Hansi Flick’s half-time message to Barcelona after comeback win over Villarreal
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 22: Eric Garcia of FC Barcelona celebrates his team's third goal, scored by an own goal by Pau Navarro (not in frame) of Villarreal CF, during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between FC Barcelona and Villarreal CF at Spotify Camp Nou on November 22, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Pablo Rodriguez/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Eric Garcia revealed Hansi Flick’s message to his players after Barcelona came from 2-0 down to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday in an eventful game. Two early goals put the visitors in charge of the match, while a missed penalty from Lamine Yamal made it feel like it simply wasn’t going to be Barca’s day. However, the champions turned it around in the second half, with Eric asked afterwards what Flick had said to his players at the break. “He told us to respect our positions and to stick to our roles. We knew that once we scored a goal, it would be very difficult to stop us,” he said. “We scored the first one, the second came almost immediately, and with our fans pushing us on at the Camp Nou, we had even more energy.” Garcia also highlighted the importance of the victory that keeps Barcelona top of the table. “It has enormous importance. Villarreal is an excellent team, and this was a complicated match after the international break, especially with the wind. Sometimes you take these matches for granted, thinking you’ll win them easily. But today reminded us that nothing is guaranteed. Every match has to be fought for from the first minute,” he added. “Villarreal is a Champions League-level team with a fantastic coach. They had two chances and scored two goals. But after that, we woke up, started playing our game, and they barely threatened us again. In the second half, we played the way we should always play.”

item.title: Ravens Report Card, Week 11: Mistakes and miscues mount in sixth straight loss
item.description: Nov 22, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd (55) tackles Baltimore Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins (2) during the fourth quarter at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens dropped their fifth consecutive game on Monday night, losing to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers by three points (23-20). Here are report card grades for the team’s position groups from another disheartening defeat in Week 10. Quarterback: C+ Jacoby Brissett made a number of good throws in this game and orchestrated five scoring drives. It was not his fault that the Ravens fumbled the ball multiple times and his pass-catchers dropped more than five passes. The veteran finished with a 24-of-37 passing line with 276 yards through the air. His touchdown pass came via a trick play to a wide-open Rashod Bateman for a 25-yard strike in the fourth quarter. Brissett was not perfect, however. He was inaccurate on some pass attempts and threw a game-sealing interception on the team’s final drive, which was an inexcusable mistake where he should have thrown the ball away. The Ravens may not have ultimately gotten down the field into position for a game-winning field goal, but there was time left to do so and Brissett’s interception cost them that opportunity. Running Back: C- It’s difficult to give a poor grade to the running backs when Derrick Henry and Justice Hill combined for 163 rushing yards, averaged over nine yards per carry and scored two combined touchdowns. However, while both were effective churning out yards on the ground, they also each lost a fumble. Hill’s fumble at the goal line negated a would-be long touchdown run in the first half that instead resulted in a touchback. Then, in the fourth quarter with the Ravens trailing by six points, Henry had the ball poked out after making a screen catch. It was a controversial call that maybe should have been ruled an incompletion, but nevertheless Henry’s ball security needs to be better. Fortunately, the Panthers did not score points off either of these turnovers — but they still costed the Ravens valuable points and possessions. Wide Receiver: C + Zay Flowers had his most productive performance in several weeks, reeling in a team-high eight receptions on 11 targets for 97 yards. He was open a lot and created yards in space on crossing routes, which has been Flowers’ bread and butter this season. He did have one drop just before halftime that would have been a long gain. Rashod Bateman started hot with 67 yards and a long touchdown catch early in the game, but only finished with two catches on six targets. Devontez Walker had a nice 34-yard grab on his only target. It was a quiet outing for Ja’Kobi Lane who was not credited with a target after receiving the most throws his way of anyone last week. item.title: ‘It just can’t happen’- Pat Freiermuth calls out DK Metcalf after Steelers ejection
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth has delivered an honest verdict on DK Metcalf’s ejection against the Philadelphia Eagles, admitting his teammate’s actions were unacceptable. Metcalf was sent off during the third quarter of Pittsburgh’s 19-16 defeat after receiving his second personal foul penalty of the game for poking Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. The incident quickly became one of the biggest talking points following the Steelers’ narrow loss, with Freiermuth making it clear that he supports his close friend but expects better from him. Pat Freiermuth sends clear message to DK Metcalf after Pittsburgh Steelers ejection Speaking to reporters after the game, Freiermuth did not attempt to defend Metcalf’s actions, despite their close relationship in Pittsburgh. “He knows that’s unacceptable,” Freiermuth said. “He’ll be fine. But like I said, he’s one of my closest friends on the team, and he knows I have his back in those situations. But it just can’t happen.” The comments offered a glimpse into how Metcalf’s behaviour was viewed inside the Steelers locker room, with Freiermuth making it clear that friendship does not excuse what happened. Metcalf’s ejection also came during another frustrating outing for the wide receiver, who managed just one reception for two yards from four targets before being sent off. The two-time Pro Bowler has struggled to find consistency this season. He has not recorded more than two receptions in a game since his 11-catch, 93-yard performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Across 10 games, Metcalf has recorded 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns from 74 targets. That represents a drop from his first season in Pittsburgh, when he finished with 59 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns across 15 games. Metcalf had already faced disciplinary trouble last season after being suspended following an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan. With Pittsburgh now 6-4 following the defeat to Philadelphia, the Steelers will need their leading receiver to find his form while avoiding further incidents. Freiermuth’s message was clear: Metcalf has the support of his teammates, but another costly moment is something the team cannot afford. item.title: 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz carted off the field in Mexico City game vs. Vikings
item.description: San Francisco 49ers offensive tackle Colton McKivitz (68) is carted off the field after an injury during the first half of an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. (AP Photo/Eduardo Verdugo) (Eduardo Verdugo/AP Photo/Eduardo Verdugo) MEXICO CITY - San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury to his lower left leg in the second quarter of their meeting with the Vikings on Sunday night and was carted off the field at Estadio Banorte with an air cast. McKivitz, 30, was bent backward when running back Christian McCaffrey was tackled into him at the end of a 4-yard run. McKivitz rolled over and emerged from the pile with his lower left leg bent at an awkward angle. Left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet to the turf and players from both teams quickly took a knee, many looking away from McKivitz, as the 49ers' medical staff raced onto the field. Williams embraced McKivitz before he was carted away as most of the team's roster was on the field to show their support. McKivitz has been among the most durable players on a team known for its chronic injury issues and was in the midst of the best season of his seven-year career. Since becoming a full-time starter in 2023, McKivitz has made 62 consecutive starts, and he entered Sunday's game without allowing a sack in 327 pass-blocking snaps this season. The 49ers signed McKivitz to a three-year, $45 million contract extension before last year's season opener. McKivitz was replaced Sunday by Vederian Lowe, 27, a five-year veteran with 25 career starts. The 49ers signed Lowe to a two-year, $9.25 million contract in March. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What a doozy of a game. No Connor Bedard , no Bowen Byram , no Elias Pettersson . Such excitement! Two of the hottest teams in the race for Landon DuPont did battle at Rogers Arena on Saturday. The Canucks must have set their alarms for 7:00, because they woke up a period late. That will give Head Coach Manny Malhotra fits, as it has happened far too often. item.description: Greenwich poses for a team photo with their championship plaque and banner after winning the CIAC State Open girls swimming and diving championship on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, at Yale. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) NEW HAVEN - The Greenwich girls swimming and diving team captured its second straight State Open title and 23rd overall Sunday by holding off second-place Ridgefield 634-617.5 at Yale. The Cardinals, under first-year head coach Megan Kelly , lost to the Tigers in the regular season before beating them by 18.5 points at FCIACs and 45.5 at Class LL. They completed the trifecta at the Open. "I'm so proud of them," said Kelly, who took over for Brendan Heller, who won four Class LL championships, three State Open titles and three FCIAC championships in five seasons as coach. "Coming in, we knew we had a lot of work to get where we were last year, which was winning the Triple Crown (conference, class and Open titles). It was really tough at the beginning of the season … but they worked really hard in the pool." The Open title was the Cardinals' fourth in the last six years. Ridgefield won crowns in 2022 and 2024. Greenwich senior Kensington Worden led the way with a dramatic victory in the 50 freestyle, touching the wall in 23.57, only .03 seconds ahead of the second-place finisher. For Worden, it was a dream come true. "Coming in as a freshman at this program, it is beyond my wildest dreams ever to become an Open champion," Worden said. "I'm just so happy." Senior Ellison Charette gave Greenwich its second individual title of the meet with a time of 4:57.33 in the 500 freestyle. After that, it was the Cardinals' depth that held off Ridgefield, which had two wins from Zsofia Milak (50.55 in 100 free and 1:50.58 in 200 free) and two from its relays (200 free and 400 free). Ridgefield's 200 free relay of Milak, Dalia Katra, Mary Kelly and Ellen Griffin broke the Open record with a time of 1:34.18. The Tigers held the previous record of 1:35.48, set in 2022. The foursome also won the 400 free relay to end the night. On Thursday, Cardinals sophomore Alden Charette defended her diving crown with a record 561.55 points. The Cardinals' game plan for Sunday was simple. "I told them before this meet, if everyone just moves up one spot individually, we can win," said coach Kelly, a Greenwich alumna and former All-American swimmer. Mission accomplished, but not without months of hard work. "It might seem like it's tiring going two and a half hours every single day, but we are all there and all doing it together, which makes it more special. ... It's full of support and love and everything in between," Worden said. Other individual winners included Norwalk/Brien McMahon's Emma Giafardino in the 200 IM (2:05.05), Weston's McKenzie Parsons in the 100 butterfly (55.54), Wilton's Vedha Kongettira in the 100 backstroke (56.45) and Brookfield's Maggie O'Hara in the 100 breaststroke (1:04.36). (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Notre Dame’s 2026 college football schedule has been called many thing over the last eight months, but “tough” or anywhere near the word “hard” was certainly not among them. Still, some have mentioned that this Irish schedule could look a lot trickier as the season progresses. While they may eventually be true, it may not matter all that much (except for message boards and social media). Notre Dame took a minute or two to get going against the Wisconsin Badgers in the season opener, but eventually the Irish whooped them 42-13. Notre Dame welcomed the Rice Owls to South Bend for the home opener, and sent them back to Texas with a 52-0 loss. Although the Irish were big favorites against Michigan State, they got their best shot — and still beat the Spartans 27-10. The Irish were once again massive favorites over a Big 10 team, and they more than covered against Purdue with a 49-10 win that was never that close. Notre Dame was better than a three touchdown favorite against North Carolina, but ran into a bit of a clunker (and rain) and beat the Tar Heels 37-26. After two weeks on the road, Notre Dame returned to South Bend and the homecooking did them well as the Irish destroyed the Stanford Cardinal 58-7. Disaster hit the Irish against BYU in a 28-24 loss, and no matter what part of the game you want to complain about (because there was quite a bit) the simplest thing to say is that Notre Dame flat out got outplayed by the Cougars. Against Navy, Notre Dame took a slower path than fans would like, but in the end the Irish won the game 35-13 and completely shutdown the Middies in the 2nd half. Notre Dame did “the thing” that fans and pundits have been waiting on, and took down No. 1 Miami in South Bend 31-24. There was no hangover from the massive win over the Canes, and the Irish whipped Boston College at home, 41-7. Notre Dame took care of business against SMU in what was kind of a weird game, but still dominating on many levels. Next up for the Irish is a trip to Syracuse for the final game of the regular season. (YURI CORTEZ/AFP via Getty Images) Several San Francisco 49ers players looked distraught, and two slammed their helmets to the Estadio Banorte field, after seeing right tackle Colton McKivitz's gruesome injury during Sunday night's game in Mexico City against the Vikings. The Niners were up 14-10 midway through the second quarter and began a drive at their own 35-yard line. McKivitz was leading a block for running back Christian McCaffrey to the right side of the field. When McCaffrey was tackled by multiple Vikings defenders, they rolled up on the backside of McKivitiz's legs. The offensive lineman's foot apparently got caught underneath the players. item.title: Bam Adebayo Says Heat Are Not Satisfied With 7-Game Win Streak Despite His Triple-Double vs. Thunder
item.description: MIAMI, FL - NOVEMBER 22: Bam Adebayo #13 of the Miami Heat looks to pass the ball during the game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on November 22, 2026 at Kaseya Center in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Eric Espada/NBAE via Getty Images) Bam Adebayo led the Miami Heat to a comfortable 123-113 win over the severely shorthanded Oklahoma City Thunder tonight. He finished with 24 points, 15 rebounds, 12 assists, two steals, and two blocks, stuffing the box score and recording a triple-double while shooting 8-11 from the field (72.7% FG) to extend the Heat’s winning streak to seven games . After the win, Adebayo spoke to the media and shared his thoughts on his performance and what the seven-game win streak means for the team. “Just making the right reads; obviously, I’ve grown from that point to now. Obviously, I’m more efficient and consistent; that was a fun game to be a part of,” Bam Adebayo said initially about his own performance tonight. Without Giannis Antetokounmpo on the floor tonight, Bam Adebayo played his original center role, where he felt he was much more efficient than at power forward. This performance ties him with LeBron James for the second-most triple-doubles for the Heat (ninth in the regular season), with only Jimmy Butler having recorded more triple-doubles in franchise history (13). But with the team just 16 games into the regular season, Bam Adebayo also said the Heat are not satisfied and should not get complacent, since they had a 3-6 start to the season before the win streak. “We’re not satisfied. I’m glad we won, but we gave up 33 in the fourth quarter. We’re trying to hold teams under 15 made threes, and they made 16. So, I’m satisfied that we’re winning, but I want to win in a way that feels like we’re dominating.” “I want to feel like, when we get out there, there’s a certain physicality and effort. I feel like we show that in sparks and segments, but not for 48 minutes. That’s the goal.” “Obviously, you enjoy winning and being on a streak, but we want to play well not just in the regular season, but deep into the playoffs,” Adebayo concluded . Bam Adebayo’s latest performance showed how effective he can be when given the freedom to operate as the Heat’s primary center. His improved efficiency and playmaking have been key to the Heat’s turnaround, but his comments suggest the team still has plenty of room to grow and no room for complacency. A seven-game winning streak is encouraging, especially after their difficult start, yet Adebayo is focused on building habits that will translate to postseason success. The Heat have improved to 10-6 following tonight’s win. Bethel (14-3-5) was playing in its first boys soccer final since 2010, when it shared the Class M title. Sunday's win gave the Wildcats their seventh state championship and first outright crown since 1996. They also shared titles in 1981 and 1982 and won outright in 1987 and 1994. Berlin (15-6-2) hadn't allowed a goal in its first four tournament games, including wins over three South-West Conference squads. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
